scope: Repair of issue and nominee details using existing ledger research; no fresh political intake or forecast recalibration.
findings: Issue players reused general biographical motives from unrelated issues and arbitrary merged donor matches, implying unsupported backing.
Long issue pages buried faction comparisons beneath generic actor biographies.
Nominee sections mismatched their labels: base was separated from backers and history/base/controversies used recursive field rendering.
Local tab state and horizontal mobile tabs made profile navigation harder to understand.
changes: Issue overview leads with policy and compact faction comparisons; separate URL-addressable players, faction disputes and real evidence chronology.
Structured issue actors preserve individual versus faction positions, inferred incentives and scoped financial relationships; external actors and specific gaps remain visible.
Candidate profiles show nomination rationale, positions with evidence, strengths/weaknesses, base with backers, dated history, controversies and research limits using explicit components.
Mobile section selector exposes every detail section; sources open contextual evidence and original candidate JSON remains downloadable.
Daily/weekly role and integrity validation maintain scoped actor coverage and financial relevance.

validation.automated: Lint, 5 TypeScript unit tests, 25 Python tests, TypeScript/Vite production build, database validation and 11 browser tests.
validation.browser: All ten issues and five candidate base/history/source views; AI unrelated-biography/donor regression; mobile 320px sections and overflow; desktop/mobile screenshot inspection.

limitations: Existing recorded research is reorganized and qualified; this UI repair does not constitute fresh external verification.
Structural validation catches missing fields and broken references, not analytical truth.
